For the test project, do this:

1. Click a contig's ID to open it, and look over its features and checks.
2. Close the window, then tick every row.
3. Press **Lock**. The app asks about CHIM01, which is flagged; choose **Lock
   anyway**.

Contigs must be locked here before they can be exported. The rest of this page
explains what you are looking at.

Each kept contig of a locked sample is one row:

![The Annotation Review table, one row per contig](figures/get-started/annotation-table.png)

The **Checks** column summarizes each contig's checks as in the Assemble step.
The Warnings, ITSx Warnings, Screen, and Chimera columns show a breakdown of each
contig check.

[Quality checks and flags](Curation-Flags.html) explains what each warning
means.

Click a contig's ID to see more details. 

![A contig: its five features, read coverage, and gene map](figures/get-started/annotation-details.png)

The window shows a table of annotated features (18S, ITS1,
5.8S, ITS2, 28S), **Sequence and read coverage**, **Edit active feature boundaries**, 
the **Reference alignment**, **Curation warnings**, the
**Chimera check**, and **Notes**. Your notes also show in the table's **User
Notes** column once you close the window.

**Sequence and read coverage** draws the contig as an interactive map: read depth,
the percentage of clipped reads, the features as arrows (dashed ends are
partial annotations), and the base pairs once you zoom in. Scroll to zoom, drag to pan, or type a
position. Clicking a gene makes it the active feature that will show up in the **Edit
active feature boundaries** and the **Reference alignment** panels below.

At the top of this window, three buttons record what you decided about a contig: **Mark Reviewed**, **Exclude
& Lock**, and **Mark Partial**.

**Lock** locks the contig and keeps the window open; **Lock & Close** locks it and
closes the window. Neither marks it Reviewed. If the contig failed some of the checks
and is not marked Reviewed, RiboPilot will print warning messages when you attempt
to lock the sample.

A locked contig is read only. To make any edits, unlock it first. 
Only contigs that are locked can be exported. Only one assembly path
can be locked per sample: paths are alternative reconstructions of the same
rDNA repeat, so a sample should only export one. However, multiple contigs
can be locked and exported for the same sample.

GenBank tends to reject submissions containing sequence outside the core 18s-5.8s-28s region.
So for a real submission, it is best to trim your contigs before export. 

To trim many contigs at once, tick them and press **Trim** in the toolbar. Choose
**Match gene ends** to keep only the annotated span, or **Gene
ends + flank** to keep a few extra bases on each side. Only contigs
with all five features (18S, ITS1, 5.8S, ITS2, and 28S) can be trimmed using this bulk trim button. To trim
partial contig, open the details window and click the "Trim Assembly" button. This button also allows you to trim the contig using a custom
range.

RiboPilot saves the original contig, so you can use the **Restore** button (or **Restore assembly** in a contig's window) 
to undo a trim.

After a trim or an edit to gene boundaries, the contig's quality flags are recalculated right away. 
BLAST, chimera checks, ITSx, and coverage results keep the values from the last pipeline run.
